## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhātuvibhaṅga* ("Analysis of the Elements") is the third chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. Alongside the preceding *Khandhavibhaṅga* and *Āyatanavibhaṅga*, it serves as a foundational analysis supplementary to the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* [Hazra 1994]. Doctrinally, the chapter provides an analytical exposition of elements (*dhātu*), incorporating a Sutta-oriented analysis (*suttantabhājaniya*) [Nguyen Van Thuong 2008]. Bhikkhu Sujato notes that the Abhidhamma *Dhātuvibhaṅga* classifies 36 elements, deriving its primary list from the *Bahudhātuka Sutta* along with elaborations drawn from the *Dhātuvibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 140), whereas the extant *Bahudhātuka Sutta* adds five further elements absent from this chapter [Sujato 2012].

Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus demonstrates dense interconnections within the Abhidhamma and canonical literature, recording over 8,000 matches across 182 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The largest internal affinities are with companion treatises of the *Vibhaṅga*—specifically the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), *Āyatanavibhaṅga* (Vb 2), *Indriyavibhaṅga* (Vb 5), *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), and *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* (Vb 18)—as well as books of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (e.g., *Dukanikkhepa*, *Dukaatthuddhāra*, and *Rūpavibhatti*) and MN 140 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the text across languages with northern Abhidharma and Yogācāra treatises, including the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, the *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra*, the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, Vasubandhu's *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, and commentaries on the *Abhidharmakośa* [DharmaNexus].
